exposure: maternal anthropometric parameters (pre-pregnancy weight, maternal height, pregnancy weight gain, pre-pregnancy body mass index)
cohort: 333 randomly selected pregnant mothers with singleton pregnancies admitted for delivery after 28 weeks of gestation at a tertiary care maternity hospital in Sri Lanka.
finding: Higher pre-pregnancy weight and pregnancy weight gain predicted better birth weight, satisfactory pregnancy weight gain was predictive of maturity at birth, and satisfactory pre-pregnancy weight and maternal height predicted a good APGAR score at birth.
